title: Sons of Immigrant Killed by ICE in Houston Demand Independent Investigation
excerpt: The family of Lorenzo Salgado Araujo and Latino civil rights leaders call for transparency after federal agents fatally shot the Mexican national during an enforcement operation in Houston's Magnolia Park.
body:
• Lorenzo Salgado Araujo, a Mexican immigrant, was shot and killed by an ICE officer during an enforcement operation in Houston's Magnolia Park neighborhood.
  • His sons and Latino civil rights leaders are demanding an independent investigation, saying federal agents claimed Araujo attempted to ram an agent with his van.
  • The killing is the latest in a series of fatal encounters involving immigration agents under the Trump administration, following high-profile shootings in Minneapolis and Texas.
  • At least six people have been killed by immigration agents since the start of Trump's second term, according to The Trace.

A Father's Final Morning

Lorenzo Salgado Araujo was in his van in Houston's Magnolia Park neighborhood when Immigration and Customs Enforcement officers approached during an enforcement operation. Within moments, a federal agent had fired on the Mexican national, killing him. Federal authorities say Araujo attempted to ram an agent with his vehicle. His family disputes that account.

https://x.com/CBSNews/status/2080833306585669705

Now Araujo's sons are demanding an independent investigation into their father's death, calling him "a hardworking Mexican man" who posed no threat to anyone. Latino civil rights leaders have joined the family in demanding transparency from federal authorities.

A Pattern of Fatal Force

The Houston killing is part of a grim tally that has grown under the current administration. At least six people have been killed by immigration agents since the start of President Trump's second term, according to The Trace, an outlet focused on gun violence.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=LRjVayC5Ds4

In Minneapolis, immigration agents fatally shot Renée Good, a mother of three, and Alex Pretti, an armed nurse with a gun permit, during separate incidents in January. Both were white, middle-class Americans protesting immigration enforcement — and their killings were broadcast in near-real time, drawing national outrage and criminal charges against at least one agent.

In South Texas, Ruben Ray Martinez, a 23-year-old US citizen, was shot and killed by an ICE agent during a traffic encounter in March 2025. His mother, Rachel Reyes, did not learn that the officer who killed her son worked for ICE until nearly a year later, when a public records request by watchdog group American Oversight exposed an internal incident report.

"He took my son's life for nothing."

— Rachel Reyes, mother of Ruben Ray Martinez

Calls for Accountability Grow

Body camera footage released in the Martinez case appeared to show federal agents standing in front of Martinez's car as it moved slowly — contradicting the official account that he rammed an officer. A Cameron County grand jury declined to indict officers in that case.

For immigrant communities, the mounting toll raises urgent questions about the use of force during routine enforcement operations. Advocacy groups argue that the administration's aggressive stance on deportations has created conditions where lethal confrontations become more likely.

Impact on Immigrant Communities

The cases have sent a chill through immigrant neighborhoods across the country. Indian Americans, while rarely the direct targets of ICE enforcement operations, have expressed concern about the broader erosion of civil liberties and the climate of fear affecting mixed-status families in their communities.
nri_angle: The pattern of fatal ICE encounters raises civil liberties concerns for all immigrant communities, including Indian Americans in mixed-status families.
